title: Primary math: fraction operations
description: Four lessons from same-denominator addition to fraction-decimal links: operate, compare, and translate between forms.
assumptions: Denominators up to 12; decimals terminate. No network or apparatus needed.
stage1goal: Build operating rules from equal parts.
same-denominator.title: Same denominator: add the parts
same-denominator.goal: Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator.
same-denominator.reading: With equal parts, only the count of parts changes: 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7; the denominator stays.
same-denominator.worked.prompt: Why does the denominator stay 7 in 2/7 + 3/7?
same-denominator.worked.fb: The parts are already the same size; only how many changes.
common-denominator.title: Make the parts match
common-denominator.goal: Rename fractions to a common denominator before adding.
common-denominator.reading: Different denominators mean different part sizes; rename to equal parts first: 1/2 + 1/4 = 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4.
common-denominator.worked.fb: Only equal-size parts can be counted together.
common-denominator.rename.prompt: 1/2 + 1/4 written in fourths: what is the numerator?
compare-fractions.title: Compare by matching parts
compare-fractions.goal: Compare fractions using common denominators or benchmarks.
compare-fractions.reading: Compare by equal parts or by benchmark 1/2: 3/5 > 1/2 because 3/5 = 6/10 > 5/10.
compare-fractions.struggle: Without computing decimals, explain how to decide whether 3/5 or 1/2 is larger.
compare-fractions.worked.fb: 3/5 is more than half of 5 parts (2.5), so above 1/2.
compare-fractions.transfer-recipe.prompt: A recipe needs 2/3 cup sugar; you have 3/5 cup. Do you have enough?
fraction-decimal.title: Fractions and decimals are one idea
fraction-decimal.goal: Translate between fractions and decimals and use both.
fraction-decimal.reading: A fraction is division: 3/4 = 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75; decimals are fractions of ten, hundred, ….
fraction-decimal.worked.fb: 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75; both name three of four equal parts.
fraction-decimal.transfer-half-of.prompt: Half of 10 meters is 1/2 × 10. How many meters?
